title: Hilary Duff ate New England clam chowder and a Dunkin’ Munchkin on stage during her Mass. concert
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Hilary Duff tried New England clam chowder and Dunkin' Munchkins on stage at Xfinity Center in Mansfield.
Duff was initially hesitant, expressing fear of trying clam chowder, a staple New England dish, during her concert.
The audience cheered as Duff tasted and enjoyed the chowder, describing the broth as 'wicked good' and delighting in the experience.

title: Adley Rutschman ready to make his debut with Red Sox on Tuesday
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman to debut with Red Sox against Blue Jays after recovering from wrist inflammation.
Rutschman acquired from Orioles on Aug. 3, played rehab games with Triple-A Worcester last weekend.
Red Sox to decide between carrying three catchers or designating Jake Rogers for assignment.

title: Springfield zoo suffers devastating damage during severe storm
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Springfield's The Zoo in Forest Park closed indefinitely after severe storm damage uprooted trees and destroyed enclosures.
A state of emergency was declared in Springfield due to severe thunderstorms causing power outages and a building collapse.
The nonprofit zoo faces financial challenges from lost revenue and repair costs, accepting donations at forestparkzoo.org.

title: 2 dead in crash on Marlborough highway
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Two people died in a multi-car crash on I-290 East in Marlborough on Monday afternoon.
Massachusetts State Police and Marlborough Fire and EMS responded to the crash before 3 p.m.
The Solomon Pond Road exit on I-290 East was closed, causing significant traffic delays.

title: Body recovered from Lake Quinsigamond in Shrewsbury
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A body was found in Lake Quinsigamond, Shrewsbury, following a report of a possible drowning.
Shrewsbury police and divers used drones and sonar technology to locate the victim near Sunset Beach.
The investigation into the drowning is ongoing, and the victim's identity has not been released.

title: Undrafted Patriots linebacker is carving out a roster spot
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Khalil Jacobs, an undrafted linebacker from Missouri, is impressing at New England Patriots training camp.
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel noted Jacobs' play speed, despite his slower 4.77-second 40-yard dash time.
Jacobs shone in an intra-squad scrimmage, making significant plays against the Patriots' starting quarterback.

title: Gov. Healey signed a law expanding abortion rights — here’s what to know
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Governor Maura Healey signed a law expanding abortion rights in Massachusetts, removing gestational limits for later pregnancy abortions.
The new law allows physicians to perform abortions based on their professional judgment, replacing previous restrictions for post-24-week abortions.
Supporters argue the law improves access for patients in complex situations, while opponents claim it reduces protections for unborn children.

title: Lost gravestone of free Black man who died in 1729 uncovered in downtown Boston
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A gravestone for Sebastian, a free Black man, was restored and is the oldest known of its kind in the U.S.
The gravestone was found at Boston's Granary Burying Ground during a conservation project led by Kelly Thomas.
Sebastian, also known as Boston, advocated for marriage rights for the enslaved and was a respected community member.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 13 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Carlton Davis and Will Campbell returned to Patriots practice, with Campbell fully participating and Davis taking part in limited fashion.
Romeo Doubs showcased his skills with a touchdown catch, while Kyle Williams impressed with a deep ball reception.
The Patriots are preparing for a joint practice with the Colts and their preseason opener against them this Thursday.

title: Lifeguard dragged underwater by white shark at Maine beach
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A lifeguard at Scarborough Beach State Park was briefly dragged underwater by a white shark during a rescue exercise.
The beach was closed for an hour while officials assessed and monitored the area after the shark encounter.
Scarborough issued safety reminders following sightings of juvenile white sharks near local beaches, urging caution to beachgoers.
